story: A five-man breakaway went clear early and stayed out front until the second lap of the Montjuïc circuit, where the peloton brought them back. From there, the racing opened up with many attacks on the later laps, with Remco Evenepoel among the most active riders trying to force a split. But as the moves kept following one another, they increasingly began to cancel each other out. The climb proved too short to create decisive gaps, allowing the front group to keep coming back together. In the final few laps, Ineos took control at the front to keep the race together for a reduced sprint. There, Brady Gilmore proved fastest, beating Dorian Godon.
